A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DyVTE research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, token-status ablations, attention analyses, and inference-speed examples for DyVTE.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds benchmark-level latency comparisons and fixed-exit attention analyses.

M1.justification: The classifier, full visual-token removal, and cross-entropy training remain. However, v1 defines the supervision threshold as reference uncertainty multiplied by 1.03, whereas v2 describes scaling the exit prediction's uncertainty and leaves the threshold unspecified. The PDFs do not resolve whether this changes label generation or is imprecise rewriting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LLaVA instruction-training data and nine evaluation benchmarks: VQAv2, GQA, ScienceQA, TextVQA, POPE, MME, MMB, SEED, and MM-Vet. Newly cited datasets are not newly evaluated; the added analyses use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds FastV, ToMe, and DyVTE+FastV comparisons for LLaVA 13B on SQA-I and MMB, where v1's 13B results compared vanilla inference with DyVTE. These methods already appeared in v1's 7B comparison, whose comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a seconds-based latency evaluation for LLaVA 13B on SQA-I/MMB and a GQA text-attention entropy comparison with exits at layers 0, 8, 16, and 24. Existing training budgets and principal benchmark settings are retained. The new timing evaluation does not specify hardware or detailed measurement procedures.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds a controlled exit-depth analysis of text-attention entropy, and Figure 1 adds attention-matrix comparisons with and without visual tokens. Existing token-status and attention-status ablations are unchanged. The exit-layer distribution analysis moves to Appendix A.3 rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: The main attention summary changes from mean-and-variance curves in v1 Figure 3 to bars without variance indications in v2 Figure 2. Appendix Figures 8–12 retain their variability bands. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes LLaVA-DyVTE 7B's MME computation from 6.3 TFLOPs (-29.2%) to 4.3 (-51.7%), retaining its 1491.4 score. Table 2 corrects EAGLE's VQA FLOPs percentage from 22.3% to -22.3%. v2 also adds latency results and fixed-exit entropy curves; the existing pruning-comparison and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly defines the modality-specific attention aggregates through explicit submatrix sums and normalization in Equation 8. This is a limited mathematical specification beyond v1's verbal description. The principal optimization equations are retained, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The three-stage inference account, dynamic visual-token exit contribution, and efficiency claims remain. v2 removes the introduction's explicit claim of FlashAttention compatibility. The highlighted 45.7% computation saving and compatibility with FastV were already reported in v1.

C2.justification: New Section 6 acknowledges that full visual-token exit may be suboptimal when some visual information remains useful in later layers. The discussion of Figure 5 also shifts from emphasizing similar entropy behavior across tasks to emphasizing task differences as motivation for dynamic exit.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 specifies attention aggregation, normalization, and max pooling across attention heads. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit statement that layer-specific hyper-networks do not share parameters. The main training hyperparameters and code-access URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The research positioning is substantially revised around more directly related visual-token efficiency work. v2 acknowledges prior visual-token withdrawal and distinguishes automatic exit selection from manual removal, while adding substantive discussion of PruMerge, G-Prune, and LLaVA-Mini. Much of v1's broader architecture and dynamic-inference survey is shortened or replaced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanation are extensively rewritten. Existing inference-pattern analyses move ahead of the method into a dedicated Section 3, exit-layer analysis moves to the appendix, and limitations and a submission checklist are added. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to one. The main attention plots become stacked bars, appendix attention grids become overlaid plots, and exit-layer plots move to the appendix. v2 removes the original DyVTE schematic, expands Figure 1 with attention matrices, and adds the fixed-exit figure and latency table.

improvement.justification: The benchmark-level latency comparison, controlled exit-depth analysis, clearer organization, and explicit full-exit limitation provide a limited net improvement in validation and clarity. Most existing results remain unchanged. The gains are tempered by ambiguous threshold wording, omitted parameter-sharing disclosure, and insufficient timing-protocol detail, so the revision does not establish a substantial overall improvement.
